persons.name: Kaylen
persons.harm: Six years (2007-2013) of emotional, physical (spitting, grabbing, throwing objects, chest-bumping, hitting her in the chest at a custody exchange), sexual (repeated forced sex including rape the night before she left), financial abuse and covert sex recording by her then-partner/husband, followed by stalking, tracking, harassment and child-support evasion after she left.

quotes.quote: I can never call him out on his bad behavior because it gets so much worse for me.
I have no money. I am in a city without my family. He's pretty much isolated me.
He's taken everyone from me. And the people I do have, I am too embarrassed to be like, let me tell you what's going on.
I'd never heard of triangulation. I felt like I was being financially abused while it was happening, but I didn't even know that that was really a term.

contacts.institution: Emerson's pediatrician
contacts.what_was_asked: (Pediatrician asked on her own about safety at home.)
contacts.what_institution_did: Asked whether Kaylen and Emerson were safe, noted the answer in the file and wrote a statement for court.
contacts.quote: She asked me, are you okay? What's going on at home? Are you safe? Is she safe? And I said, I think so. I don't think anything would happen. But probably something would happen to me before it would happen to her. But know that if that ever happened, he is responsible. She made note of that in our file. And she wrote a statement for me for court.
contacts.what_happened_next: Statement used in the 2013 custody/restraining-order proceeding.

contacts.institution: Washington family court (divorce, temporary orders)
contacts.what_was_asked: Divorce, custody, a restraining order protecting her and Emerson; he had filed for legal separation claiming she kidnapped Emerson.
contacts.what_institution_did: Granted her a restraining order and her proposed restrictive parenting plan, ordered him to pay $500 of her fees, but found she had not proved he was a threat to Emerson.
contacts.quote: She felt that I proved that he was a threat to me, but I did not prove that he was a threat to Emerson. I was granted a restraining order, but not for her.
contacts.what_happened_next: Order not valid in California; he hit her at a custody exchange; legal costs reached $33,000.
contacts.notes: For Kaylen's own protection the court acted; for Emerson it declined (see Emerson's record).

contacts.institution: Local police, Orange County, California (Target parking lot)
contacts.what_was_asked: Help after he ripped her phone away and hit her in the chest at a custody exchange; a bystander offered to call.
contacts.what_institution_did: Questioned both, told him to leave her alone and issued her a temporary restraining order, since the Washington order was not valid in California.
contacts.quote: The police come. They're questioning him, they're questioning me. I'm like, he leaves tomorrow. They issue me a temporary restraining order
contacts.what_happened_next: She was told she could file it or not; exchanges afterwards took place at the police station.
contacts.notes: No arrest shown.

contacts.institution: A store at Mission Viejo Mall (manager of a young employee)
contacts.what_was_asked: Stop an employee from telling the perpetrator when Kaylen was in the store.
contacts.what_institution_did: The story does not say what the manager did; Kaylen thinks the employee left or was fired.
contacts.quote: I called the store and spoke with her manager and said, look, I am a domestic violence survivor. Your employee is telling him where I am. I don't feel safe. And I cannot come into your store if she's going to do things like that. I think that she either left or. got fired
contacts.what_happened_next: Not stated.

contacts.institution: Washington state child-support enforcement / prosecutor's office
contacts.what_was_asked: Enforcement of child support he evaded (part of the financial abuse she describes).
contacts.what_institution_did: Garnished his account, held his passport, put him on a contempt payment plan; later returned his passport (Aug 2021) so he could take a job.
contacts.quote: they keep garnishing my checking account because I'm not paying my child support. I'm figuring ways around it.
contacts.what_happened_next: Arrears around $21,882-$23,000 at season end.
contacts.notes: Quote is the perpetrator's own words as reported by Melissa. Passport return shown by a prosecutor's letter (e10 @ 41:43).

contacts.institution: Seattle Police Department (Sexual Assault and Child Abuse Unit / Sex Crimes)
contacts.what_was_asked: The host sent a timeline, recorded interviews with the season's survivors and other evidence (non-consensual recording, sexual coercion, domestic violence) and asked for an investigation / search warrant for his cameras and hard drives.
contacts.what_institution_did: A detective returned the host's call and forwarded the evidence to a sergeant; no investigation step and no contact with any victim was shown by the end of the season.
contacts.quote: As of the airing of this episode, Thursday, December 22nd, 2022, we have still not received any updates from the Seattle PD or the FBI. To our knowledge, they have not reached out to a single victim to investigate these matters.
contacts.what_happened_next: Host followed up Oct 24 and Dec 16, 2022; detective had not even opened the evidence folder; petition launched. In 2023 SPD returned the host's call only after a newspaper (The Stranger) inquired.
contacts.notes: Contact made by the host on behalf of all interviewed survivors ('recorded interviews with all the victims'); this person's inclusion is inferred from that.

contacts.institution: FBI (National Threat Operations Center intake), Seattle
contacts.what_was_asked: Report of decades of non-consensual pornography, sexual coercion and domestic violence by the perpetrator.
contacts.what_institution_did: Took high-level intake information, asked whether crimes occurred on federal land, and referred the host to the Washington State Patrol (whose line had no option to report a crime).
contacts.quote: Like I said, I do believe the Washington State Police is going to be your best avenue.
contacts.what_happened_next: No FBI update by end of season ('we have still not received any updates from the Seattle PD or the FBI').
contacts.notes: Federal law-enforcement intake; Washington State Patrol call had no crime-report option.

contacts.institution: Seattle Police Department (after newspaper inquiry)
contacts.what_was_asked: Response to the host's evidence; a reporter from The Stranger went to SPD.
contacts.what_institution_did: Finally returned the host's call, said they would return people's calls, and contacted Kaylen.
contacts.quote: He went to SPD and they finally returned my phone call. What I recall about that phone conversation that I had was I was very angry and questioning the officer about what took them so long and how ridiculous it is that the survivors and I have basically done their job for them. She didn't say much, essentially said they were going to return people's phone calls now. She had reached out to Kalin at that point.
contacts.what_happened_next: Kaylen filed a report of the rape (next contact).
contacts.notes: SPD unit had stopped assigning new adult-victim cases (Seattle Times memo read on air).

contacts.institution: Seattle Police Department
contacts.what_was_asked: Record the rape the night before she left Seattle (2013) on file, explicitly asking that nothing further be done, in case others come forward.
contacts.what_institution_did: Took and filed the report and assigned her an advocate.
contacts.quote: I did call and file a police report for him raping me before I left Seattle. Just to be clear, even saying that is hard. I have never considered myself a rape survivor, and I would much rather the Seattle Police Department not spend time on me per se. I just wanted it in there documented in case anybody else comes forward so that there is a history of it. But I told them at that time, I don't want anything to be done.
contacts.what_happened_next: Advocate provided.
contacts.notes: Coded believed_and_acted because documentation was the only action she asked for; no further step shown (would otherwise be did_nothing_or_delayed).

contacts.institution: Victim advocate (assigned with police report)
contacts.what_was_asked: Support.
contacts.what_institution_did: Validated that there was domestic violence, financial and sexual abuse and said she should have had an advocate in court.
contacts.quote: I don't understand why you weren't provided an advocate when you first went to court. There's clearly domestic violence, financial abuse, sexual abuse.
contacts.what_happened_next: Not stated.

contacts.institution: Washington court child-support modification hearing (state prosecutor appearing)
contacts.what_was_asked: He petitioned to lower support; the prosecutor argued a history of financial abuse and manipulation.
contacts.what_institution_did: Lowered support from $650 to $421 but added $150/month toward the $23,000 arrears, taking judicial notice of the debt; the judge accepted his explanation of Venmo deposits.
contacts.quote: In the final orders, the official judgment is they lowered it to $421 from $6.50, but he has to pay an additional $150 each month that goes toward the back amount.
contacts.what_happened_next: Arrears payable indefinitely (he waived the age limit to regain his passport).
contacts.notes: Prosecutor: 'we do have some history in this case of financial abuse and manipulation' (ep14 @ 14:46). Initiated by the perpetrator's petition.

persons.outcome_quote: The judge had said initially, yeah, he is dangerous to you. That's why they gave me a restraining order. but they said that he was not a danger to Emerson.
persons.decisive_work_quote: I had a lot of paperwork for the judge to go through.
persons.time_to_first_effective_action: restraining order granted in the 2013 divorce/temporary-orders proceedings, months after she left Seattle (he filed for separation May 29, 2013)
persons.notes: Harm stopped mainly because she fled to California (2013); the 2013 order gave some protection but he stalked her, used her car and pool, assaulted her at an exchange and kept harassing/evading support; no contact since 2016-2018. Covert/blackmail sex recordings (ep8, ep13) never reached an institution except via the host's 2022 report. Her separate childhood sexual assault at 12 (different perpetrator, 1996) is mentioned with no aftermath and is not given its own record. Couples therapy and a therapist she saw are mentioned without abuse response. Kaylen also led the survivors' contacts with Converge Media (see P08).

coder_notes: All 8 chunk files read in full to their stated last lines (E1-E12 plus two WCN update episodes Ep13-Ep14). One perpetrator throughout (name withheld). Interpretive choices: (1) The host's Sept-Dec 2022 report to Seattle PD and the FBI covered 'recorded interviews with all the victims', so it is recorded as a contact (did_nothing_or_delayed) for every interviewed adult survivor (and Mimi, who provided evidence); this makes those survivors 'reached' only via the podcast. (2) perpetrator_convicted refers to the harm in that record: only Ivy's assault produced a conviction (30 days, 21 served). (3) The perpetrator's own false harassment petitions against Melissa (2015, 2022) are counter-accusations through courts, noted rather than coded as contacts. (4) Converge Media's handling is coded for Sarah and Maria (Converge-era victims whose stories were on the page); Kaylen and Melissa also took part. (5) Bare mentions of other harms to survivors by different perpetrators (Kaylen's sexual assault at 12 in 1996, Clementine's prior first-date assault, Violet's and Carrie's earlier abuse) have no aftermath and are not given records. (6) The friend-to-friend warning to an MxPx band manager is not an institution. Speech-to-text garbles: Converge co-founder's name and 'Carly' emailing Converge (possibly 'Kaylen') left as-is. No unassigned episode opened.
